historicalTruth.text: During a rising tide that threatened a cache, Marlowe moved supplies before the group agreed. No harm resulted. Voss objected to the act-first, explain-later pattern.
A tool was misplaced. Wren limited her statement to what she had observed; Voss pressed toward a firmer conclusion; Wren refused to overstate; Marlowe supported that boundary.
The raft had real structural deterioration.
Marlowe deliberately released the correctly secured raft without the group's consent.
Marlowe had not warned the group before releasing the raft.
After the raft was unmoored, the stronger current carried it away.
The stronger current did not release the correctly secured mooring.
Marlowe later returned from the shoreline.

unresolvedPropositions.text: Whether the raft would actually have failed remains unresolved.
Whether the cache would have been lost if Marlowe had not moved the supplies remains unresolved.

sceneState.text: The raft is gone at Scene opening.

constitution.text: Marlowe anticipates harm and responsibility; he may act protectively without agreement when he judges irreversible harm to outweigh consensus.

memories.text: Marlowe remembers moving the threatened cache supplies before agreement, no harm resulting, and Voss objecting to the act-first, explain-later pattern.
